audit_scope.description: This batch covers EL topics (EVM memory operations, system instructions CREATE/CALL/SELFDESTRUCT, Paris merge transition, Istanbul gas repricing, Prague fork block processing, transaction type handling) and CL topics (EIP-7688 SSZ container migration for stable merkleization). Also includes application-layer EIP-5749 wallet provider injection.

in_scope: Transaction Processing (type decoding, validation, signature recovery)
P2P Gossip Validation for SSZ Containers

misclassified_entities.reason: Internal EVM component, not an external entity. The opcode dispatcher is part of the EVM execution engine itself.
Internal EVM state, not an external entity. The execution context is part of the EVM runtime.
Internal smart contract logic consuming CHAINID opcode, not an external entity sending data into the system.
Internal EVM entity. A contract calling a precompile is within the EVM execution boundary.
Internal system-level address used for beacon root and history storage system transactions. Not an external entity — it is a protocol-defined internal mechanism.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Submitter via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any user or DApp can submit transactions via public JSON-RPC. No authentication required. Transactions may be malformed, have invalid signatures, incorrect nonces, or attempt resource exhaustion. Covers 'Transaction Sender', 'Transaction Submitter', and 'Transaction Signer' entities from source subgraphs.

trusted_external_entities.name: Blob Data Submitter via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: JSON-RPC API (eth_sendRawTransaction with Type 3 blob tx)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Submits EIP-4844 blob transactions containing VersionedHash commitments. Unauthenticated, all blob data and KZG commitments must be fully validated.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Producer via P2P / Engine API
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P block propagation / Engine API newPayload
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Block producers submit blocks containing ordered transactions, state roots, and requests. When received via P2P, fully untrusted. Full block validation (header, transactions, state transition) is required.

trusted_external_entities.name: Consensus Layer via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The CL communicates with the EL via JWT-authenticated Engine API. The channel is authenticated, but payload content (execution payloads, fork choice state) must still be validated by the EL. Covers 'Beacon Chain Consensus Layer' and 'Beacon Chain' entities from source subgraphs.

trusted_external_entities.name: Beacon Chain Validator via P2P Gossip
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P Gossip Network (beacon block proposals, attestations)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Validators propose blocks and submit attestations over unauthenticated P2P gossip. Any validator may be malicious — proposing invalid blocks, conflicting attestations, or attempting censorship. Covers 'Beacon Chain Validator' entity.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peer via Gossip (SSZ Containers)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peers send SSZ-encoded containers (using EIP-7688 ProgressiveContainer format) over gossip. Containers must be validated for correct field structure, stable merkle roots, and proof integrity. Unauthenticated channel.

trusted_external_entities.name: Off-Chain Verifier (Merkle Proof Consumer)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External systems verifying merkle proofs against beacon state. They consume proofs but do not send data into the system. However, proof requests could be crafted to target edge cases in the ProgressiveContainer merkleization.

trusted_external_entities.name: Smart Contract Verifier (On-Chain Proof Consumer)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Smart contracts that verify SSZ merkle proofs on-chain. They rely on stable generalized indices from EIP-7688. Untrusted — contracts may supply malformed proof data.

trusted_external_entities.name: Wallet Browser Extension via window.evmproviders
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Browser extensions inject wallet providers into the page via window.evmproviders. Any extension can inject, potentially including malicious ones. SVG icon data must be sanitized to prevent XSS. No authentication mechanism.

trusted_external_entities.name: DApp User via Browser
trusted_external_entities.rationale: DApp users interact with wallet providers through browser APIs. User actions trigger wallet selection and provider interaction. Untrusted browser environment.

trusted_external_entities.name: Hardware Wallet Implementation
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Hardware wallets sign SSZ containers. EIP-7688 migration affects container structure which hardware wallets must handle correctly. External device with its own firmware — data sent to/from it crosses a trust boundary.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node via P2P (devp2p)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Archetypal attack vector: peer nodes on the P2P network can send invalid blocks, invalid transactions, or attempt eclipse attacks. All data from peers is untrusted.

trusted_external_entities.name: MEV-Boost Relay / External Builder
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Archetypal attack vector: external MEV relays and builders can provide incorrect block data, censor transactions, or perform denial of service. Unauthenticated external service.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full transaction validation required: signature recovery (ECDSA), nonce check, gas limit validation, EIP-7623 calldata floor cost, intrinsic gas calculation, init code size limit (EIP-3860), transaction type decoding, and balance sufficiency check.
Must validate VersionedHash format, KZG commitment integrity, blob gas pricing, and all standard transaction validation. Blob count limits must be enforced.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: P2P block reception / Engine API newPayload
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full block validation: header validity (parent hash, gas limits, base fee calculation), transaction list integrity, state root verification after applying all transactions, withdrawal processing, request aggregation (deposits, withdrawals, consolidations).

JWT authentication verified. Payload content must still be validated: execution payload structure, block hash consistency, state transition correctness. Paris merge constraints enforced (difficulty=0, nonce=0, empty ommers).
Validate proposer signature, slot assignment, attestation validity, slashing conditions. Reject duplicate or conflicting attestations.
Validate SSZ container structure per EIP-7688 ProgressiveContainer rules. Verify stable generalized indices, active field bitmask, and merkle proof consistency across fork transitions.
Proof verification must handle ProgressiveContainer generalized indices correctly. Edge cases in container migration (active fields vs inactive fields) must not produce invalid proofs.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: On-chain SSZ merkle proof verification (EVM call)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Smart contract must receive valid proof data. Generalized indices must remain stable across forks per EIP-7688. Malformed proof inputs must not cause EVM execution anomalies.
Provider registration must validate provider object structure. SVG icon data must be sanitized to prevent XSS. Object.freeze must be applied to prevent provider list tampering.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: EIP-5749 wallet discovery and selection API
boundary_edges.security_assumption: User wallet selection must be validated. DApp must not be able to override user preference or inject fake providers.

Hardware wallet must correctly interpret EIP-7688 ProgressiveContainer format. Signed data must match expected container hash. Migration from one container version to another must not break signing compatibility.
All blocks and transactions received via P2P must be fully validated. Eclipse attack mitigations required. Peer reputation scoring should limit impact of malicious peers.
Block bids from relays must be validated for correctness. Relay-provided execution payloads must pass full EL validation before inclusion. Censorship resistance mechanisms should be considered.
